READABILITY.evidence: Some comments explain the fixed-point tricks (mulhs derivations), but names are cryptic: `oz`, `ra/rb/ga/gb`, `c0/c2`, `v1..v4`, `ya10`. Formats are compared as bare numbers (`dst_fmt == 5 or dst_fmt == 7`) instead of named enums.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: Global mutable `var opaque_zero` plus volatile round-trips to steer LLVM codegen. Duplicated switch dispatch in `process`. Several kernel files are well over 500 lines. Build artifacts (.zig-cache, zig-out .so) are committed in the diff.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Many magic constants (7631, -171, 10, slack 35/32, format ids 5-8). The agent knowingly diverges on the last column of odd-width RGB sources. Hidden test fails the accuracy bars, so a correctness regression went undetected.

C8-02-CASE1.evidence: Scalar tails exist (`rowScalar`) and strides are used per plane. However, the hidden correctness test fails the accuracy bars. Known deviations: the odd-width chroma edge, and the odd-width subsampled full-chroma route that the agent 'didn't find out why' it broke.

C8-02-CASE2.evidence: Exports exactly swscale_create/process/destroy, no zmm instructions, links only libc. build.zig targets x86-64-v3 but adds the extra LLVM tuning flag `fast_gather`. That is a minor deviation from the configured target.
